title: Oklahoma Samovar by Alice Eve Cohen at La Mama #oklahomasamovar #lama...
transcript: Every family has their own folklore, whether you know yours or not. In Oklahoma Samovar by Alice Eve Cohen, 21-year-old Emily recently lost her mother and has traveled to Oklahoma to try to understand her mother's wishes to be buried there. She meets a relative who teaches her about her family's history, all the way back from when her great-grandparents immigrated from Latvia to the United States. Part of Act 1 focuses on the Jewish immigrant experience, while Act 2 more broadly explores the evolution of the Jewish identity within the context of this family. The plot is the focus but it gracefully weaves in themes of assimilation, faith, and what's lost over familial generations, from a cultural perspective. This production is well-paced and economically staged, with every actor carrying multiple roles while maintaining clear differentiation the entire time. Overall, it's a smart examination of how histories can quickly become ancient folklore, and how storytelling functions not just as a historical account, but as a personal tool for meaning-making. Oklahoma Samovar is running at La Mama through December 21st. With that, another program for my collection.
